picks.title: Meet Martini: A Film Set for AI Video That Aims to Help Filmmakers Streamline Their Shots
picks.headline: Meet Martini: A Film Set for AI Video That Aims to Help Filmmakers Streamline Their Shots
picks.excerpt: Martini is a collaborative, web-based platform pitched as a virtual 'film set' for AI video production: filmmakers get real cinematic controls — fly around a 2D/3D scene and operate a virtual camera to find coverage — instead of prompt-roulette with generative video models. It doubles as a real-time collaborative pre-production hub with NLE-compatible timeline and XML export, launching freemium with paid tiers from $15/month.
picks.rationale: A concrete new craft tool: a Figma-like virtual film set that swaps prompt-roulette for real camera/coverage controls and exports XML to Premiere/Resolve — directly changes how filmmakers and DPs approach AI-video shots. Fresh, distinct, and net-new to the movies section.

picks.title: The rise of the independent AI-assisted developer tools: warnings and considerations
picks.headline: The rise of the independent AI-assisted developer tools: warnings and considerations
picks.excerpt: ProVideo Coalition's Jeff Greenberg examines the flood of small, AI-assisted independent tools now entering post-production pipelines, sorting them into 'Gold Rush' profit plays vs genuine 'Problem Solver' utilities. He lays out five questions editors and facilities should ask before trusting one on client work — maintenance if the developer vanishes, API/platform compatibility, documented failure conditions, credential/data security, and update cadence — arguing that in a craft where reliability is the product, unvetted AI tools are accumulated risk.
picks.rationale: A practitioner's decision framework — five concrete questions to vet AI tools before they touch client work — that changes how editors and post facilities adopt the wave of small AI utilities tomorrow. High actionability, credible craft voice, distinct angle from the tool-release stories.
